subject: Complex numbers
title: Real and Imaginary Parts, and Equality
subtitle: Why one complex equation is two real ones, and how to solve equations in z, its conjugate and its size, up to olympiad level.
prerequisite_note: Chapters 1 and 2; simultaneous linear equations; absolute value and square roots of real numbers.
objectives: Prove that the standard form a + bi is unique.
Use Re and Im as functions, knowing which rules they obey and which they break.
Solve equations in z, its conjugate and |z| by comparing parts, without losing or inventing solutions.
Decide when az + b z̄ = c has one solution, none, or infinitely many.
Read an equation in z as curves in the plane: one real condition gives a curve, two give points.
Solve functional equations over the complex numbers by substitution, including the degenerate cases.
Express the qubit averages ⟨X⟩ and ⟨Y⟩ as the real and imaginary parts of one complex number.

theorems.statement: uniqueness of the standard form a + bi
az + b conj(z) = c is uniquely solvable iff |a| ≠ |b|

quantum_links.summary: ⟨X⟩ = 2 Re(conj(α)β) and ⟨Y⟩ = 2 Im(conj(α)β); a qubit has 2 real parameters after normalisation and global phase.

reviewer_type: AI review with automated symbolic and numerical checks; no human mathematician review yet
